label: early copy steps (outputting tokens 1-2) in long sequences, token-gated
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, almost entirely on the 2nd and 3rd output steps (recall_idx 1: 68% of mass, recall_idx 2: 27%). It is weak on the delimiter step and essentially never fires in the original phase or late in the copy. Rate rises steeply with sequence length (L=9 holds 47% of mass; L<=5 is rare), so it acts like an early-copy, many-outputs-still-to-go detector (to_go 5-7). Top activations come at recall_idx 1, where the input is orig(0) and many outputs remain. Within that window it fires on only about 10% of steps, so precision is low. Which steps fire depends on token identity: the current and next outputs being tokens like z, e, 0, b, f, q, c raise the rate about 3-6x. No simple token set captures this (best token-gated F1 was about 0.28). Magnitude was not checked beyond these position trends.
